source.title: Robustness to Pruning Predicts Generalization in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Lorenz Kuhn; Clare Lyle; Aidan N. Gomez; Jonas Rothfuss; Yarin Gal

page_placements.theme: Double descent in held-out losses beyond zero-one error
Complexity proxies track some risk curves without a universal effective-complexity test

record.tranche_reason: The study performs width sweeps and reports double descent in test loss for deep networks, but uses cross-entropy test loss rather than the test-error curve specified by the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-loss double descent in its own experiments. Comparisons of generalization measures, including effective dimensionality and pruning measures, are not separate results about the claim's test-error curve. It does not report an explicit test-error fall-rise-fall curve or locate a peak relative to the interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: The study uses double descent only as a testbed. It reuses the Maddox et al. (2020) width-sweep setup (the Nakkiran CNN and ResNet18 on CIFAR-100) to check whether prunability and baseline measures rank-correlate with test loss. The reported results are those measures' Kendall correlations. The double-descent curve itself is shown only for cross-entropy test loss, in figures, with no test-error curve and no location of the interpolation threshold. No version is tested on its own terms: V1 names test error, and V2, V3, V5, V6 and V7 are not addressed. The reader's 'tests/T2' contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that prunability is highly informative of generalization on the DEMOGEN models. In the test-loss double-descent setting, they find it rank-correlates with test loss better than effective dimensionality and other baselines (CNN τ=0.3613), though margins beat it on ResNet18. They make no claim about the existence or shape of double descent itself beyond observing it in test loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates width sweeps on CIFAR100 and reports cross-entropy test loss, rather than reproducing the original test-error measurements. It does not report the interpolation threshold location.
record.method_sensitivity: The experiments cover two architectures, CNN and ResNet18; the text says the ResNet18 results are consistent with the CNN results. No change in curve behavior by another tested condition is stated.

fits_no_version.finding: In width sweeps of a CNN and a ResNet18 on CIFAR-100 (200 epochs, standard augmentation, no added label noise stated), the authors report that cross-entropy test loss shows double descent. These are figures only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-wise double descent appears in cross-entropy test loss for CNN/ResNet18 width sweeps on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Prunability (fraction of weights kept under magnitude pruning) shows a double-descent shape across width. It rank-correlates with test loss (CNN τ=0.36; ResNet18 τ=0.48) more strongly than Hessian effective dimensionality (τ=-0.02; 0.13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pruning-based complexity measure tracks the model-wise double-descent test-loss curve better than Hessian effective dimensionality.

record.problems: The double-descent curves are reported only as plots, without numerical curve values. The text does not locate the peak relative to the interpolation threshold. The main experiment uses 5 random seeds; the number of seeds for the ResNet18 experiment is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bearing on the claim versions were reported. Baseline-measure comparisons and pruning-versus-random-perturbation results were not extracted because they do not report the claimed test-error shape.

untested.parts: No test-error curve over width is reported (only test loss), and no peak location relative to the interpolation threshold.
Only deep networks; no other model classes.
No test of whether one complexity measure predicts peak location across axes. Prunability is assessed only by rank correlation with test loss along width.
Label noise, multiple peaks and regularization tuning are not varied.
The test-loss curve is not re-plotted against an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Kendall τ of generalization measures with test error (as opposed to test loss) in the double-descent sweeps. For the CNN, Frobenius norm gives τ=-0.54 and negative sum of train losses gives τ=-0.94 against test error. This indirectly suggests test error may fall largely monotonically with width while test loss shows double descent, but no test-error curve is shown, so this cannot be confirmed.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 1 (ResNets on CIFAR-10) shows test error decreasing with width. It is described as an illustration only, with no setup details, so no row was made. Rows left out (DEMOGEN correlations, pruning vs random perturbation) correctly do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The reported width-sweep curves are for cross-entropy test loss; the study does not report the claimed test-error curve or the peak's location relative to the size that just fits the training set.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
No increase in training sample size near an interpolation threshold is tested.
The study's double-descent experiments use deep network architectures, not a sweep across model classes; the reported curve is test loss.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across size, epochs, and sample-size axes.
The study does not test label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The study does not measure the curve against an effective parameter count or test whether that makes the descent an ordinary U-shape.

relation.reason: Double descent serves as an evaluation setting for generalization measures. The reported test-loss curves do not directly test a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study uses a previously established double-descent setting to evaluate prunability and competing generalization measures. Its substantive comparisons concern their correlations with test loss; it does not establish the interpolation-threshold relationship required by V1.

source_check.notes: Figures 2/4 and 5 give test-loss correlations of 0.3613/0.4812 for prunability and -0.0197/0.1272 for effective dimensionality; the statement rounds correctly. Observed states describe test-loss double descent only. A.4 and A.5 reference different ResNet18 implementations; B.1 points to A.5.
